cards.summary: The browser asks for a page

prompt.text: The browser asks the server for a page with an HTTP

answer.text: The browser asks the server for a page with an HTTP request.

hints: Name the message the browser sends.
cards.fullLine: The browser asks the server for a page with an HTTP request.

teaching.text: The server answers with a response: a status, headers and a body.

teaching.alt: Browser and server exchanging a request and a response

teaching.search: How Browsers Work Explained DOM CSSOM Render Tree
teaching.alt: A walk through the browser's rendering pipeline, from HTML to pixels

prompt.text: What does the browser build from the HTML it receives?

answer.text: A tree of objects that JavaScript can read.

hints: The name has three letters and stands for an object model.
cards.fullLine: The browser builds the DOM from the HTML it receives.

teaching.text: HTML describes the page; the browser turns those tags into objects that scripts can change.

prompt.text: DNS turns a host name into an

answer.text: DNS turns a host name into an IP address.

hints: Two letters, short for Internet Protocol.
cards.fullLine: DNS turns a host name into an IP address.

teaching.text: Without DNS the browser would not know which machine to contact.

prompt.text: Which one runs a page's JavaScript?

hints: It is the same place where layout and clicks are handled.
cards.fullLine: A page's JavaScript runs on the main thread.

teaching.text: A long script keeps clicks and paints waiting until it finishes.

prompt.text: CSS rules become a second tree, the

answer.text: CSS rules become a second tree, the CSSOM.

hints: It ends with the same three letters as the DOM.
cards.fullLine: CSS rules become a second tree, the CSSOM.

teaching.text: That second tree holds the parsed style rules, and scripts can read or change them.

cards.summary: Two trees make the render tree

prompt.text: The render tree is built from which two trees?

hints: One side is structure, the other is style.
cards.fullLine: The render tree is built from the DOM and the CSSOM.

teaching.text: Only content that will be shown reaches the render tree.

answer.text: After layout, the browser paints the pixels.

hints: One word: what an artist does with a brush.
cards.fullLine: After layout, the browser paints the pixels.

teaching.text: Painting comes after layout has decided where every box sits.

prompt.text: Which step decides where each box goes?

hints: A viewport change makes this step run again.
cards.fullLine: Layout decides where each box goes.

teaching.text: When the viewport or content size changes, positions and sizes are recomputed.

hints: Nothing can be styled before the page is parsed.
cards.fullLine: The order is parse, DOM, styles, layout, paint.

teaching.text: Parsing comes first; styling and layout need the DOM.

cards.summary: Page script uses the main thread

prompt.text: Page JavaScript usually runs on the browser's

answer.text: Page JavaScript usually runs on the browser's main thread.

cards.fullLine: Page JavaScript usually runs on the browser's main thread.

teaching.text: A Web Worker runs script somewhere else, so the page stays responsive.
